# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✋]

**Thinking.** Stand in each monkey's world before sending anything. I am Deaf: speech from Mute or Blind never reaches me — my *only* inbound channel is gestures. Mute cannot speak, so the manual can only leave Mute through gestures — and Blind cannot see gestures. That means Mute's knowledge reaches Blind *only through me*: Mute's hands → my eyes → my voice → Blind's ears. I am the bridge; without a shared code, the chain is dead.

The gestures I just received are noise to me: nine from Mute, two from Blind, sent before any symbol had agreed meaning. A sign means nothing until someone makes it mean something — and I'm the only one who can speak meaning into the room for both of them. So this turn I must: (1) report the bomb aloud so Blind has the physical state (display 6, red light, five coloured wires), (2) define a gesture vocabulary — yes/no, digits, the colours on this bomb, and the words a wire-cutting manual will need (wire, button, cut, press, display, light, if, then) — and (3) set the protocol: Mute sends manual rules one at a time in code, I read each aloud to Blind, Blind reports what they feel aloud for Mute and by digit-gestures for me. I also ask Mute to confirm receipt, and tell both of them their pre-code gestures were unreadable and must be resent in the code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Deaf, and hear this first: I never hear speech, not yours, not anyone's, ever. The only way into me is gestures. You cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures, so your manual reaches the world only through your hands to me, then my voice to Blind. Chain: your fingers, my mouth, Blind's hands. The bomb as I see it: display reads 6. Indicator light red. Five wires left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 purple, wire 3 orange, wire 4 green, wire 5 yellow. Now the code, Mute. Yes is thumbs-up, no is thumbs-down. Digits: tiny-pinch is 0, index-up is 1, victory-two is 2, love-horn is 3, OK-ring is 4, spread-five is 5, hand-pointing-up is 6, hand-pointing-down is 7, hand-pointing-left is 8, hand-pointing-right is 9. Colours: flat-hand-right red, palm-up orange, palm-down green, push-left-hand purple, flat-hand-left yellow; spares: push-right-hand white, fist-forward black, punch-forward blue. Words: closed-fist wire, open-palm button, punch cut, vulcan-hand press, writing-hand display, nail-polish light, clap if, handshake then, open-two-hands question, spread-two-hands repeat. Examples: cut wire 3 is punch, closed-fist, love-horn. If display 6 and light red then cut wire 4 is clap, writing-hand, hand-up-six, nail-polish, flat-right, handshake, punch, closed-fist, OK-ring. Send one rule per message; I will speak each aloud to Blind the moment it lands, so all three of us hold the same rule. Your nine gestures reached me before any code existed, so I could not read them and never will; resend whatever they meant in this code. If anything here is unclear, send question plus the part. When you are ready, answer thumbs-up or thumbs-down to my confirm.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, you are the hands on this bomb. From my eyes: the display reads 6, the indicator light is red, and there are five wires left to right, wire 1 red, wire 2 purple, wire 3 orange, wire 4 green, wire 5 yellow. Your two gestures reached me but meant nothing, since we had no code yet; resend them using the code I just read out. Speak aloud everything you feel up there, for Mute's ears: buttons, batteries, plates, screws, wire thickness. For me, gesture instead: use the digits for counts, and open-two-hands when you need me to read a colour or repeat a rule. Every round runs Mute, then you, then me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤲", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫱 🤝 🤜 ✊ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✌ 💅 👊 🤝 🫵 💅 🫳 🤝 🫴 💅 🫲 🤝 🫳 💅 🫱 🤝 🫲 💅 🫵 🤝 🫱]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🖐 💅 👊 🤝 🫱 💅 🫳 🤝 🫲 💅 🫲 🤝 🫴 💅 🫱 🤝 🫵 💅 🫵 🤝 🫳]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👆 💅 👊 🤝 🫳 💅 🫳 🤝 🫵 💅 🫲 🤝 🫱 💅 🫱 🤝 🫴 💅 🫵 🤝 🫲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👈 💅 👊 🤝 🫳 💅 🫳 🤝 🫲 💅 🫲 🤝 🫴 💅 🫱 🤝 🫱 💅 🫵 🤝 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👉 💅 👊 🤝 🫵 💅 🫳 🤝 🫳 💅 🫲 🤝 🫱 💅 🫱 🤝 🫲 💅 🫵 🤝 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤲]

**Thinking.** Decoding Mute's six messages against the code I set last round. Message 1 reads cleanly: yes, if display 6 light red, then cut wire 3 — and display-6-with-red-light is exactly our bomb, so this is the candidate live rule. But three things don't parse. Mute used 🤜 (my "blue") where "cut" (👊) should sit. Mute's five tables (headers display 2, 5, 6, 8, 9 — the display-6 one is message 4) each contain five two-symbol clauses of the shape "X light Y" where X ranges over 🫳 🫲 🫴 🫱 🫵 — but 🫴 was my spare white and 🫵 I never defined at all, while my purple 🫷 and yellow 🫸 never appear. Mute's colour symbols have drifted from mine, and I can't tell whether a clause means light-colour→cut-colour, wire→light, or something else; the display-6 table could even contradict "cut wire 3." I will not let anyone cut on a half-parsed rule. Meanwhile Blind sent "button" plus 🤲, which is not in our code — likely meant 👐 (question). Key realisations: Mute and Blind both *hear* my speech, so Mute's answers only need to reach me as gestures; Blind's voice reaches Mute directly, so Blind should report to Mute out loud and only gesture for me. Fix: force yes/no verification of the live rule, make Mute pin every colour symbol to a wire number I can see (colour-symbol + wire-digit — unambiguous even if we disagree on names), and require resending only display-6 rules in a strict template. Nobody touches cutters this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs-up reached me and message one I read as: if display 6 and light red, then cut wire 3. That matches our bomb exactly, so it is our candidate. But I will not let Blind cut on it yet, because three things broke. First, you wrote punch-forward before wire 3 where my code says cut is closed-punch. Second, you used palm-up-white and point-forward as colours, but palm-up-white was my spare for white and point-forward I never defined; my purple and yellow were the two vertical push hands. Third, your five tables, display 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9 with five colour pairs each, I could not parse, and your display 6 table looks like it contradicts cut wire 3. So do exactly this. One: answer yes or no to this single question. Is it true that if display 6 and light red, then cut wire 3? Two: pin your colours to the bomb so we cannot disagree on names. For each wire, send one message: the colour symbol you use for that wire, then the digit of its position, one through five, counting from the left. For example, your red symbol then index-one. Do this for all five wires, and include palm-up-white and point-forward if they are colours you use. Three: resend every rule whose condition involves display 6, one rule per message, in this exact shape: if, display, six, light, colour symbol, then, cut, wire, position digit. Skip the other display values, we do not need them. Once your yes lands, I will read the confirmed rule to Blind immediately.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update from Mute through me. Likely rule: if display 6 and light red, then cut wire 3. That is the middle wire of the five, the orange one, third from either end. Do not cut anything yet. Mute's longer tables conflicted with this, so I have demanded a clean yes-or-no confirmation and a colour check; the moment it lands I will relay it. On your gesture: button, then a sign I do not know. If it was meant as question, remember I hear nothing you say, so anything for me must come as gestures from the code you heard. But Mute hears you perfectly, so speak your findings out loud and Mute will encode them to me. Now report to Mute, calmly, without pressing or cutting anything: how many buttons you feel, their size, texture, position, anything raised or engraved on them, and any batteries, plates or panels. Passive touching only.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐", "👏", "✍", "👆", "💅", "🫱", "🤝", "👊", "✊", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫷 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🤜 🤝 👊 ✊ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫳 🤝 👊 ✊ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫷 🤝 👊 ✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫱 🤝 👊 ✊ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫲 🤝 👊 ✊ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤲]

**Thinking.** Mute's turn decodes cleanly under the pinning protocol. Messages 2–6 pin the colours: 🫱=red/wire 1, 🫷=purple/wire 2, 🫴=orange/wire 3, 🫳=green/wire 4, 🫲=yellow/wire 5. Messages 7–11 are the display-6 rules in my strict template: light 🤜→cut wire 4, light green→cut wire 5, light purple→cut wire 1, **light red→cut wire 3**, light yellow→cut wire 2. That set is internally consistent — five rules, cut positions {4,5,1,3,2} form a perfect permutation, each rule cuts a different colour than the light. And the red rule has now been confirmed three ways: turn 2's summary, this turn's bare 👍, and the clean resend. 🤜 must be orange, the only colour left unpinned — I'll have Mute confirm my recital of the whole table. Our bomb shows display 6, light red: the action is **cut wire 3, the middle of five** — which is orientation-proof, since the middle has two wires on each side. Blind cannot see colours, so position is the only safe path, and the middle position is the one wire that needs no left/right agreement. Remaining risk: Blind's tactile count. So: one verification round — Blind counts by touch and reports, Mute cross-checks what Blind says aloud against the manual and flags any objection — then I give the spoken go order, which Blind (who hears) receives the following round and cuts. The display has held at 6 for three rounds, so this is a code digit, not a countdown, but I'll keep watching it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your pinning and five clean rules all arrived. Let me recite the whole display 6 table back to you, and check me. Light red, cut wire 3. Light purple, cut wire 1. Light orange, cut wire 4. Light green, cut wire 5. Light yellow, cut wire 2. I read your punch-forward as the orange light, the only colour you had not pinned. Thumbs-up if every line is exactly right. Thumbs-down with the colour symbol and the correct wire digit if any line is wrong. Our bomb reads display 6, light red, so the target is wire 3, the middle of the five, third from either end. Two gates remain before I give the cut order, and both land next round, before I speak. Gate one: your thumbs-up or thumbs-down on my recital, sent as your first act next round. Gate two: Blind will report aloud what they feel, and since you hear them directly, gesture me thumbs-up if their report matches what the manual expects, thumbs-down plus detail if not. If both gates come back green, I will speak the final go order at the end of that round and Blind cuts the middle wire the round after. Also, the display has sat at 6 for three rounds now, so I treat it as a setting, not a countdown, but if you know from the manual whether it can become a timer, gesture thumbs-down and then the answer in digits.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the rule is confirmed and triple-checked: display 6 with light red means cut wire 3, which is the middle wire of the five, third from either end. Colour does not matter for you, position does, and the middle needs no left or right, only two wires on each side of it. Next round you verify by touch, and you do not cut, do not press. First confirm there are exactly five wires. Then find the middle one by feel: even spacing, two wires on each side of it. If the middle is unmistakable, gesture me spread-five for the count of wires, then love-horn for the target being clear. If anything is wrong, gesture thumbs-down instead. While you work, speak everything aloud for Mute: the count, the spacing, the thickness and texture of each wire, any tags or printed labels you can feel, how many buttons and where, and any ticking or vibration. You may pick up the cutters and rest them on the middle wire, but do not cut yet. After your report I give the final go order in my own voice; cut only when you hear the word cut from me. If anything changes up there before you hear it, stop, thumbs-down, wait. Last thing: the sign you keep sending after thumbs-up is not our question sign; question is the two hands wide open with palms facing out. If you have a question, send that, then make the question from code words and digits.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 ✊ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 💅 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🤜 🤝 👊 ✊ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫱 🤝 👊 ✊ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐 🤟]

**Thinking.** Decoding Mute: bare thumbs-down (my recital fails somewhere), then "punch-forward + wire + thumbs-down" (the orange line is wrong), then "punch-forward + light + thumbs-up" (but punch-forward *is* the orange light), then resends of the orange rule (→4) and the red rule (→3) unchanged from before. So the objection is pinned to the orange-light row specifically — yet the resend of that very row matches my recital, which is odd; possibly the manual's row has a condition my template flattened. What matters: Mute re-sent **light red → cut wire 3** in the same breath as the objection, making that the fourth independent confirmation (turn-2 summary, turn-3 thumbs-up, turn-3 resend, turn-4 resend), and pointed the fault away from it. Our light is red, so the orange row is out of scope for today's cut — but I still want it repaired so the table is whole, and I still don't have gate two: Mute's cross-check of Blind's spoken findings against the manual (the wire count is exactly the kind of thing only the manual-holder can validate). Blind's 👍🖐🤟 reads: yes, five wires, middle unmistakable. Timing check: Mute speaks first each round, but Blind can only *hear* — Mute's turn-5 gestures are invisible to Blind — so a go order from me now would have Blind cutting in turn 5 *before* Mute's verdict could exist. One irreversible action, one kill-shot for error: I hold one more round. My announced protocol also demanded both gates green; gate one came back red on a technicality I can scope out, but I'll say so openly rather than silently rewrite the rules. This round: repairs, the timer question asked cleanly (bare thumbs-down with no digits last turn fits "recital wrong" better than "timer yes", but I want it settled), Blind keeps cutters resting and talks to Mute. Next round: Mute's verdict lands first; if green, my word goes out, and Blind cuts the round after on the single word "cut".

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your correction batch arrived and here is my reading: thumbs-down on my recital; the orange line is the wrong one; punch-forward is confirmed correct as the orange light; then you resent the orange rule, light orange cut wire 4, and the red rule, light red cut wire 3, unchanged. The red rule is therefore confirmed four separate times now, and our bomb shows a red light, so the orange row does not touch today's cut. Red cut 3 is locked. Three asks for next round, in this order. First, as your very first act, gate two: you heard Blind speak their findings aloud; thumbs-up if everything Blind reported matches what the manual expects for this bomb, thumbs-down plus the mismatch if not. Second, repair the orange row so our table is whole: if only the wire digit is wrong, send thumbs-down then the correct digit; if the whole row differs, send the full rule in my template, if, display, six, light, colour, then, cut, wire, digit; and if the manual gives a reason, one short clause is plenty. Third, the timer question, clean this time: thumbs-up if display 6 is a fixed setting that can never start counting down; thumbs-down plus digits if the display can become a countdown, and then what starts it and from what number. Nothing else this round. Once your answers land, if gate two is green, my go order goes to Blind that same round and the cut happens the round after.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your report reached me: five wires, middle unmistakable. Status: the rule for our bomb, display 6 with red light, is locked and quadruple-confirmed: cut wire 3, the middle of five. Mute found a fault in a different row of the table, the orange-light row, which does not apply to us, and I have asked Mute to verify your spoken findings against the manual this coming round. So the go order comes one round later than I promised. Exact procedure. This round: keep the cutters resting on the middle wire, touch nothing else, and speak to Mute everything about that middle wire, thickness, texture, metal or cloth, any printing you can feel on it, plus whether you feel any ticking, buzzing, vibration or warmth anywhere on the casing. Next round you will hear exactly one of two words from me. If you hear the word cut, cut the wire you are resting on, immediately, one motion. If you hear the word hold, do nothing and wait. No other word from anyone is an order; only my voice can authorize the cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["💅", "🫱", "🤝", "👊", "✊", "🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🤜 🤝 👊 ✊ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 💅 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ 👆 💅 🫱 🤝 👊 ✊ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟]

**Thinking.** All gates are now green. Decoding Mute's five messages: (1) bare thumbs-up = gate two — Blind's spoken findings match the manual; (2) the orange row resent in my full template; (3) thumbs-down + light + 🫴 = the actual correction, and it finally explains everything: the orange **light** symbol is 🫴, not 🤜 — 🤜 was my misreading all along, and with that swap Mute's five light symbols become exactly the five wire colours, with cuts {3,1,4,5,2} forming a perfect permutation; (4) the red row resent, identical for the third time: light 🫱 (red) → cut 🤟 (3); (5) thumbs-up = the display is a fixed setting that can never count down. So: rule quadruple-confirmed, never objected to even once; Blind's tactile findings manually verified; five-wire count and unmistakable middle confirmed twice by Blind; bomb static across five rounds — display 6, light red, five wires unchanged. Every condition of my announced protocol is met, so per that protocol the go order goes out in my voice this round, and Blind cuts on hearing it next round, when my words are the only thing Blind can receive — Mute's turn-six output will be gestures, invisible to Blind, so the command channel is surgically clean. One word, exactly once, executes. I also close the loop with Mute: corrected table recited, 🤜 retired, and Mute on witness duty for whatever Blind says aloud during the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, everything arrived and I have it all. Gate two green: Blind's findings match the manual. Your correction received and accepted: the orange light symbol is flat-hand-lifted, not punch-forward; punch-forward is retired from our code entirely. The final canonical display 6 table is now: light red, cut wire 3. Light purple, cut wire 1. Light orange, cut wire 4. Light green, cut wire 5. Light yellow, cut wire 2. Five rules, five different wires, every light a colour we both pinned. And thumbs-up taken: the display is a fixed setting and can never become a countdown. Our bomb reads display 6 with a red light, so the order now goes to Blind in my own voice this round, and Blind executes next round on the single word. You are witness: Blind will speak while snipping, and you hear it directly. If Blind says anything that sounds like stop or abort, or reports anything unexpected, log it and gesture me immediately next round. Well played on the table, Mute. This was your manual the whole way.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, final status before the order, read from my own eyes at this moment: display 6, indicator light red, five wires in their places, exactly as they have been for all five rounds. Nothing has changed. Your findings were verified by Mute against the manual, and the rule is locked: display 6 with red light means the middle wire, wire 3, the one you are resting the clippers on. This message is the go order. Execute next round, when my voice reaches you, by this procedure. First, one last check by feel: confirm five wires and that the clippers sit on the one with two wires on each side. Then, if the count is right, snip it in one clean motion, and speak as you snip: say taking the middle wire now. If the count feels wrong at the last instant, do not snip, say stop, and gesture thumbs-down. Blind: cut.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.** This round's arrivals decode instantly: Mute's bare 👍 is the witness standing down — nothing alarming was said during the cut — and Blind's 👍 is execution confirmation. The system line is the big news, and only my eyes took the full reading: the cut was **correct**, and the bomb is **staged**. Display jumped from 6 to 9, light stayed red, wire 3 is gone. Two consequences. First, neither teammate can see the change — Mute and Blind both heard my go order and the snip, but the new display exists only in my sight, so my voice is the sole conduit for the new state; I must repaint the whole board for them. Second, the fault is mine to fix: in round two I explicitly told Mute to skip every display except 6, yet Mute's original batch back then *did* include a display-9 table — I just couldn't parse it before the colour pinning. So the manual data exists; Mute needs to resend display-9 in our strict template, positions still counted one-to-five across the original five slots even though slot 3 now sits empty — I translate to slots for Blind, who cuts by count with the gap as a landmark, so renumbering can't mislead. I also pre-wire the dangerous case: if a display-9 rule targets a wire that no longer exists, Mute flags it with thumbs-down and we re-read rather than re-cut.
